The cream surface at the left of the image is the north wall seen at a grazing angle, while the white surface is the east wall, and the gray mass filling the lower right is the south side, consistent with it lying south of the current position. I check the corner where cream meets white against the known NE room corner coordinates, and the predicted pixel position (~171) matches the observed value (~165) closely enough to confirm the pose is correct. Now I want to work out the base line and extent of the gray mass itself.
answer: Pose check: the cream/white vertical seam at u≈165 matches the predicted NE room corner column (171). Reducing the mass.

from PIL import Image; import numpy as np, math
im=np.asarray(Image.open('observations/obs_0162.png').convert('RGB')).astype(int)
R,G,B=im[:,:,0],im[:,:,1],im[:,:,2]
px,py=1.300,7.400
def bp(u,v,z=0.0):
    D=(1.55-z)*256.0/(v-256.0); L=D*(u-256.0)/256.0
    return (round(px+D,3), round(py-L,3), round(D,2))
gb=((B-R)>=4)&(R<200)
def runs(col):
    idx=np.where(col)[0]
    if len(idx)==0: return None
    g=[]; s=idx[0]; p=idx[0]
    for i in idx[1:]:
        if i!=p+1: g.append((int(s),int(p))); s=i
        p=i
    g.append((int(s),int(p))); return g
for u in [230,240,244,246,248,250,252,256,280,320,360,400,440,480,511]:
    print(u, runs(gb[:,u]))
print('--- tan floor')
tan=(R>120)&(R<200)&((R-B)>10)
for u in [170,180,200,220,240,246]:
    c=np.where(tan[:,u])[0]
    print(u, (int(c.min()),int(c.max())) if len(c) else None)
print('--- east wall base? white bottom')
wh=(R>250)&(G>250)&(B>250)
for u in [180,200,220,240]:
    c=np.where(wh[:,u])[0]; print(u,int(c.max()))
print('pred east wall base row x=3.93:', round(256+1.55*256/(3.93-px),1))
" 2>/dev/null
